title: DNS and Reverse Proxies
summary: How a name becomes an address, and how one front door hides and protects many backends.
keyPoints: DNS resolves names through a hierarchy of caches and authoritative servers.
TTL controls how long an answer is cached, so it also controls how fast changes spread.
DNS routing can be weighted, latency-based, geographic, or failover-based.
A reverse proxy terminates TLS, routes requests, compresses responses, and hides backends.
A load balancer spreads traffic across similar servers; a reverse proxy presents one front door.

complexity.note: The common case after the first lookup.
Distance and cache misses add latency.
Keep the proxy close to the app.
More flexible and more expensive than layer 4.

commonMistakes: Assuming a DNS change is instant instead of waiting for cached answers to expire.
Relying on DNS failover as if it reacted as quickly as a load balancer.
Caching personalized responses at a shared edge without varying by user and authorization.
Treating a reverse proxy as a security boundary while leaving backends reachable from the internet.
interviewNotes: State the TTL and what it means for failover and migration time.
Separate the name-resolution path from the request path; they fail differently.
Explain why TLS terminates at the edge and whether traffic is re-encrypted internally.
Choose layer 4 or layer 7 explicitly and justify the cost.

checkYourself.question: Why does a low DNS TTL help during failover?
checkYourself.answer: Caches discard the old address sooner, so clients are more likely to ask for the new one. The trade is more lookup traffic and slightly more latency.

checkYourself.question: What does a reverse proxy do that a simple load balancer may not?
checkYourself.answer: It can present one front door for routing, TLS termination, compression, caching, static files, and request limits, even when there is only one backend.

checkYourself.question: When is layer 4 a better choice than layer 7?
checkYourself.answer: When you only need to forward TCP or UDP traffic and do not need to inspect or route by application content. It is simpler and cheaper per byte.
